newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DAVIS HOMERS FROM BOTH SIDES TO LEAD ROYALS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DAVIS HOMERS FROM BOTH SIDES TO LEAD ROYALS.

text.p: The chili was hotter than usual in Kansas City on Saturday.
Chili Davis homered from both sides of the plate, driving in five runs, to lead the Kansas City Royals to a 10-4 rout of the Texas Rangers.

Batting from the right side, Davis hit a three-run homer to left field in the fourth inning off southpaw Darren Oliver to give the Royals a 5-1 lead. He then turned to face righty Matt Whiteside in the sixth and hit a two-run homer to right field for a 7-3 advantage.
Davis has homered from both sides 10 times in his career, tying him with Mickey Mantle for second on the all-time list. Eddie Murray has done it 11 times.
"It's one of the most exciting feats in baseball," said Davis, who has 306 homers in his career.
"It hasn't lost it's impact of me," he said, adding: "I'm not going to do it anymore because Eddie (Murray) is one of my favourite players."
Jim Pittsley (1-4) finally managed his first major league win in his seventh start, allowing three runs and four hits over seven innings with six strikeouts.
Pittsley allowed a two-run homer to Juan Gonzalez in the sixth inning. Ivan Rodriguez added a solo homer for Texas in the eighth off Randy Veres.
Oliver (3-7) took the loss, yielding six runs and seven hits in five innings.
In Chicago, Harold Baines's single with one out in the bottom of the 11th inning scored Dave Martinez and lifted the White Sox to a 1-0 victory over the Baltimore Orioles.
White Sox closer Roberto Hernandez (4-1) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win, Chicago's fifth in six games.

Neither team got a runner to third base until the bottom of the ninth when Cleveland loaded the bases. But Armando Benitez struck out Albert Belle and got Baines to ground into a double play to force extra innings.
The Orioles loaded the bases in the 10th and 11th, but Hernandez struck out Roberto Alomar swinging to end the threat in the 10th and Jeff Reboulet grounded into a double play in the 11th.

In New York, David Wells pitched eight scoreless innings and Charlie Hayes snapped a scoreless tie with a two-out RBI double in the seventh and scored on a single by Mark Whiten to lead the Yankees to a 2-0 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Wells (7-3) allowed just four hits, walked none and struck out eight to earn his third straight win. Mariano Rivera worked a perfect ninth with two strikeouts for his 18th save, tied for tops in the majors.
Milwaukee's Scott Karl (2-7) allowed just two hits through six innings before the Yanks scored twice in the seventh.
In Toronto, Robert Person allowed one run and five hits over 7 2/3 innings and Carlos Delgado homered for the fourth consecutive game as the Blue Jays beat the Oakland A's 3-1.
Person (1-4), who retired 13 straight batters between the first and sixth innings, walked one and struck out eight.
Delgado tied a club record with his solo shot off Oakland starter Steve Karsay in the fourth. Ruben Sierra also homered for Toronto.

In Boston, Bartolo Colon survived seven shaky innings to notch his first major-league victory and Matt Williams snapped an 0-for-14 slump with his 14th homer as the Cleveland Indians beat the Red Sox 9-5.
Colon (1-2) allowed four runs and eight hits in seven innings, walking two and striking out five in his fifth start.

The Indians took an early 4-0 lead on two-run homers by Dave Justice and Jim Thome. Williams added a solo shot in the fifth that made it 8-4 after Boston got back-to-back homers from Darren Bragg and Wil Cordero in the third. Jeff Frye also homered for the Red Sox.

In Detroit, Justin Thompson won for the fourth time in his last six starts and Raul Casanova hit a two-run homer in the second inning as the Tigers ended a three-game losing streak with a 3-1 win over the Seattle Mariners.
Thompson (6-4) allowed just one run and five hits in eight innings and struck out nine, including Ken Griffey three times after striking him out the last three times they met up.
"Nobody has had that type of mastery over Junior," impressed Seattle manager Lou Piniella said.

At Minnesota, Brad Radke tossed a six-hitter for his first complete game of the season and five different hitters had at least two hits to pace a 13-hit attack as the Twins beat the Anaheim Angels 6-1.
Radke (5-5) scattered five singles and a double but lost his shutout bid in the ninth when Tim Salmon singled home Darin Erstad with two out.
Ron Coomer had a pair of RBI hits and Paul Molitor doubled and scored twice for the Twins.
